additional_info.subject: RE: 0479588 - ID0479588-DC/Si-D/NO- [Multi] Present output control mode for converters changed for this outlet CRM:00472000557
additional_info.body:
I have use randomly the charger 2o1E11 for this example.
RSRQ (Reference Signal Received Quality): -20 dB (No signal)
RSRQ measures the quality of the received signal, taking into account both the signal strength and the interference from other cells. A value of -20 dB, labeled as "No signal," is extremely poor. This means that even with good signal strength (RSSI), the quality of that signal is so low that your device is struggling to make sense of it.
SINR (Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio): -3 dB (No signal)
SINR is arguably the most important metric for data throughput and connection stability. It directly measures how much stronger the desired signal is compared to all the interference and noise. A SINR of -3 dB, also labeled "No signal," is terrible. A positive SINR is generally needed for a stable connection. A negative value means the noise and interference are stronger than the actual signal you want to receive.
So base on this information, my suggestion here would be to try a different network operator and see if the performance improves or not.
From our side I don't see what we could do more.
